areas.season: Hot humid summers (29-30 °C), cold winters around 0 °C with some snow; spring and autumn the best; the Christmas lights from late November to early January.
areas.sleep: Midtown Manhattan for the first visit; Lower Manhattan or Brooklyn for quieter evenings.

items.name: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
items.book: Ferry tickets from Statue City Cruises (the only official ferry); pedestal and crown tickets sell out weeks ahead
items.why: The ferry from Battery Park to the statue of 1886 and to Ellis Island, where 12 million immigrants entered America between 1892 and 1954.

items.name: 9/11 Memorial, Wall Street and the Brooklyn Bridge on foot
items.why: The two pools where the towers stood, the Financial District, then across the 1883 bridge to DUMBO for the skyline.

items.name: Central Park and the Met
items.why: The 341-hectare park drawn by Olmsted and Vaux, then the Metropolitan Museum, one of the largest art museums in the world, on its edge.

items.name: Times Square, Grand Central and the city from above
items.book: Timed tickets for the observation decks; sunset slots sell first
items.why: The lights of Times Square, the vault of Grand Central, the Public Library, and the skyline from the Empire State, Top of the Rock or Summit.

items.name: The High Line to Chelsea Market and Hudson Yards
items.why: A freight railway 9 m above the street turned into a 2.3 km garden walk, from the Meatpacking District to the Vessel.

items.name: Greenwich Village, SoHo and Chinatown
items.why: Washington Square, the brownstones of the West Village, the cast-iron fronts of SoHo, dumplings in Chinatown.

items.name: A Broadway show
items.why: Forty theatres around Times Square; the TKTS booth sells same-day tickets at a discount.

items.name: Christmas in Midtown: the Rockefeller tree and the windows
items.why: The tree and the skating rink at Rockefeller Center, the lit windows of Fifth Avenue's stores.

areas.season: Cold snowy winters (-5 to 3 °C), warm summers (26-28 °C); the autumn colours in October.
areas.sleep: Back Bay or the North End; Cambridge near Harvard.

items.name: The Freedom Trail
items.why: A red-brick line through 4 km of the Revolution: Boston Common, the Old State House, Faneuil Hall, Paul Revere's house, Old North Church, to Bunker Hill.

items.name: Harvard and Cambridge
items.why: Harvard Yard, the oldest college in America (1636), and the bookshops and cafés of Harvard Square; MIT a short walk away.

items.name: The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
items.why: A Venetian palazzo built around a garden court; the empty frames of the 1990 theft, still unsolved, hang where the paintings were.

items.name: A Red Sox game at Fenway Park
items.why: The oldest ballpark of the major leagues, opened in 1912, and its 11 m Green Monster wall.

items.name: Whale watching on Stellwagen Bank
items.why: Humpbacks feeding on the marine sanctuary off Cape Ann, by boat from Long Wharf.

items.name: Salem
items.why: Half an hour by train: the town of the 1692 witch trials, its sea captains' houses and the Peabody Essex Museum; packed in October.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (31 °C), cold winters around 0 °C.
areas.sleep: Old City or Center City, near Rittenhouse Square.

items.name: Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell
items.book: Free timed tickets for Independence Hall, booked online for a small fee in the busy months
items.why: Where the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the Constitution (1787) were signed, and the cracked bell across the lawn.

items.name: The Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Rocky Steps
items.why: One of the great art museums of America, up the 72 steps Rocky Balboa ran in 1976.

items.name: Reading Terminal Market and a cheesesteak
items.why: The 1893 market hall under the old railway terminal: Amish stalls, roast pork and cheesesteak sandwiches.

items.name: Elfreth's Alley and Old City
items.why: The oldest lived-in residential street in America, from the 1700s, Betsy Ross's house and Christ Church.

items.name: Eastern State Penitentiary
items.why: The 1829 prison of solitary confinement, now a ruin you walk through; Al Capone's cell kept as it was.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (31-32 °C), cool winters (0-8 °C); the cherry blossoms in late March or early April.
areas.sleep: Downtown or Dupont Circle; Georgetown for the evenings.

items.name: The National Mall and its memorials
items.why: From the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial past the Washington Monument, the White House, the World War II and Vietnam memorials; best at dusk.

items.name: The Smithsonian museums
items.book: Some museums give free timed passes online, the African American History museum the most sought
items.why: Free museums side by side on the Mall: Air and Space, Natural History with the Hope Diamond, and the National Museum of African American History and Culture.

items.name: The Capitol and the Library of Congress
items.why: A tour under the dome of Congress, then the painted reading room of the largest library in the world.

items.name: Arlington National Cemetery
items.why: The graves of 400,000 Americans across the Potomac, Kennedy's eternal flame and the changing of the guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

items.name: The cherry blossoms around the Tidal Basin
items.why: About 3,700 cherry trees, a gift from Tokyo in 1912, in bloom for a week or two in late March or early April.

items.name: Georgetown
items.why: Federal-style houses older than the capital, the C&O Canal towpath and dinner on the Potomac waterfront.

items.name: Mount Vernon
items.why: George Washington's plantation house over the Potomac, 25 km south, with the quarters of the people he enslaved.

areas.season: Cold snowy winters (-7 to 0 °C) with the falls half frozen; warm summers (27 °C); the boats run about May to early November.
areas.sleep: Niagara Falls, New York, by the state park; the Canadian side has the view of the whole Horseshoe (passport).

items.name: Niagara Falls State Park and Goat Island
items.why: The oldest state park in America (1885): Prospect Point, Terrapin Point on the edge of the Horseshoe, the rapids from the Three Sisters islands; the falls lit every night.

items.name: Maid of the Mist
items.why: The boat into the spray at the foot of the Horseshoe Falls, running since 1846; a poncho is handed out.

items.name: Cave of the Winds
items.why: Wooden decks at the foot of the Bridal Veil Falls, close enough to be soaked.

items.name: The Canadian side and Journey Behind the Falls
items.why: Across the Rainbow Bridge on foot for the full view of the Horseshoe from Table Rock and the tunnels behind the water.

items.name: The Winter Festival of Lights
items.why: Light displays along the Canadian side and the falls lit in colour, from mid-November to early January.

areas.season: Summer 24-27 °C with the sea at 18-21 °C in July and August; quiet and grey from November to April, many places shut.
areas.sleep: Chatham or Orleans in the middle of the Cape; Provincetown at its tip.

items.name: The beaches of the Cape Cod National Seashore
items.why: Sixty kilometres of Atlantic dunes from Nauset to Race Point, Nauset Light and Marconi Beach; seals off the shore.

items.name: Provincetown and a whale watch
items.why: The artists' town where the Pilgrims first landed in 1620, and the boats to the humpbacks of Stellwagen Bank.

items.name: Great Island trail
items.why: Soft sand and pine woods out to the end of a spit in Wellfleet Bay; check the tide for the last stretch.

items.name: Cycling the Cape Cod Rail Trail
items.why: A paved old railway line of 35 km from Dennis to Wellfleet, past ponds and cranberry bogs.

items.name: Sandwich, the oldest town on the Cape
items.why: Founded in 1637: the glass museum, the grist mill and the boardwalk over the salt marsh.

areas.season: Summer 26 °C by the sea, cold winters around 0 °C; the mansions open all year.
areas.sleep: The harbour or Bellevue Avenue.

items.name: The Gilded Age mansions
items.why: The summer 'cottages' of the Vanderbilts and the Astors; The Breakers of 1895 has 70 rooms over the Atlantic.

items.name: The Cliff Walk
items.why: A public path of 5.6 km between the mansions' lawns and the rocks of the ocean.

items.name: Ocean Drive
items.why: Sixteen kilometres along the rocky shore, past Brenton Point and the summer houses.

items.name: A sail on Narragansett Bay
items.why: The harbour of the America's Cup from a schooner, in the sailing season.

areas.season: Summer 24 °C and cool nights, the colours in early-mid October; the Park Loop Road and Cadillac's summit road shut from December to mid-April and Bar Harbor mostly closes for the winter.
areas.sleep: Bar Harbor; Southwest Harbor on the quiet side of the island.

items.name: Sunrise on Cadillac Mountain
items.book: Vehicle reservation for the summit road from late May to late October, released online
items.why: The highest point of the Atlantic coast of America (466 m), the first sunrise in the country from October to early March.

items.name: The Park Loop Road and the Ocean Path
items.why: Sand Beach, Thunder Hole booming at mid-tide and the pink granite of Otter Cliff along a 3 km path by the sea.

items.name: Jordan Pond and its popovers
items.why: A 5 km loop round the clear lake under the two Bubbles, then tea and popovers at the Jordan Pond House.

items.name: The Beehive
items.why: Iron rungs and ledges up a cliff over Sand Beach; not for those afraid of heights.

items.name: The carriage roads by bike
items.why: 72 km of broken-stone roads closed to cars, built by John D. Rockefeller Jr., with seventeen stone bridges.

items.name: Lobster on the Bar Harbor waterfront
items.why: A lobster dinner or a lobster roll by the harbour, walking to Bar Island at low tide.

areas.season: Summer 25 °C in the valleys but often freezing and windy on Mount Washington; the foliage from late September to mid-October; ski season about December to March.
areas.sleep: North Conway, or Bretton Woods under Mount Washington.

items.name: Up Mount Washington by the Cog Railway or the Auto Road
items.why: The highest peak of the Northeast (1,917 m), where a gust of 372 km/h was measured in 1934; the cog railway of 1869 climbs to the top.

items.name: The Kancamagus Highway
items.why: 56 km through the national forest from Conway to Lincoln, past the Swift River and covered bridges; one of the famous foliage drives in late September and early October.

items.name: Flume Gorge in Franconia Notch
items.why: Boardwalks through a granite gorge 240 m long with walls 20-27 m high.

items.name: The Franconia Ridge loop
items.why: One of the classic hikes of the East: 14 km and 1,100 m up over Little Haystack and Lafayette, above the trees on a narrow ridge.

items.name: Skiing at Bretton Woods or Wildcat
items.why: New Hampshire's largest ski area under Mount Washington, or Wildcat's steep runs across Pinkham Notch.

items.name: Covered bridges and North Conway
items.why: The 19th-century wooden bridges of the Saco valley and the old station of the Conway Scenic Railroad.

areas.season: Summer 24 °C, cold snowy winters; the schooners sail from late May to early October.
areas.sleep: Camden by the harbour.

items.name: Mount Battie over Camden harbour
items.why: The view over the harbour and the islands of Penobscot Bay that Edna St. Vincent Millay wrote about, by a short climb or the summit road.

items.name: A day sail on a windjammer
items.why: Camden is the home port of the fleet of old wooden schooners that still sail the bay.

items.name: Rockland: the breakwater and the Wyeths
items.why: A walk of 1.3 km out on the granite breakwater to its lighthouse, and the Farnsworth museum of three generations of Wyeths.

items.name: A lobster roll on the harbour
items.why: Maine's sandwich, at a shack by the boats.

areas.season: Summer 26 °C, cold snowy winters (-8 to 0 °C).
areas.sleep: The Old Port.

items.name: Portland Head Light
items.why: The lighthouse on the rocks of Cape Elizabeth, first lit in 1791, in Fort Williams Park.

items.name: The Old Port
items.why: Brick warehouses and cobbled streets on the working waterfront, with one of the best small food scenes in America.

items.name: The ferry to Peaks Island
items.why: The island ferry across Casco Bay, then a walk or a bike ride round the island.

areas.season: Summer 27 °C, cold snowy winters; the Gorge Trail is open about mid-May to early November.
areas.sleep: Watkins Glen at the foot of Seneca Lake, or Ithaca.

items.name: The Gorge Trail of Watkins Glen
items.why: Nineteen waterfalls in under 3 km of stone stairs and tunnels cut into the gorge.

items.name: Wineries along Seneca Lake
items.why: Riesling country: tastings on the slopes over the deepest of the lakes.

items.name: Taughannock Falls
items.why: A single drop of 65 m, taller than Niagara's, at the end of a flat gorge walk near Ithaca.

areas.season: Summer 27-30 °C in the valley, cooler on the ridge; the colours in mid-late October; Skyline Drive closes for snow and ice in winter and the lodges open about April to November.
areas.sleep: Luray in the valley, or Skyland and Big Meadows lodges on the ridge in season.

items.name: Skyline Drive
items.why: 169 km along the crest of the Blue Ridge with 75 overlooks over the Shenandoah valley, at 35 mph.

items.name: Dark Hollow Falls
items.why: The park's most visited waterfall, 2.2 km there and back, steep on the way up.

items.name: Hawksbill, the highest summit
items.why: The top of the park at 1,235 m, with its stone platform over the valley.

items.name: Old Rag
items.book: Day-use ticket from March to November on recreation.gov
items.why: The famous rock scramble of the East: a 15 km loop through granite boulders to a 1,001 m summit.

items.name: Whiteoak Canyon
items.why: A string of six waterfalls down a hemlock canyon, a steep climb back up.

items.name: Luray Caverns
items.why: The largest caverns of the East, with a stone 'organ' that plays the stalactites.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (32 °C) with afternoon storms, mild winters (6-16 °C); hurricane season June to November; spring the loveliest.
areas.sleep: The historic peninsula south of Calhoun Street.

items.name: Rainbow Row, the Battery and the old city
items.why: Pastel 18th-century houses, the single houses with their side porches, the gas lamps of the French Quarter and the sea wall of the Battery.

items.name: Fort Sumter
items.why: The ferry to the island fort where the first shots of the Civil War were fired on 12 April 1861.

items.name: A plantation on the Ashley River
items.why: Middleton Place or McLeod: gardens and oaks, and the lives of the enslaved people who worked them told without varnish.

items.name: The Angel Oak
items.why: A live oak on Johns Island several centuries old, its branches spreading over a third of a hectare.

items.name: Lowcountry food
items.why: Shrimp and grits, she-crab soup and Gullah cooking in one of the best food towns of the South.

items.name: Folly Beach or Sullivan's Island
items.why: The beaches twenty minutes from town, with the sea warm from May to October.

areas.season: Hot humid summers, mild winters; hurricane season June to November.
areas.sleep: The historic district on the Beaufort River.

items.name: Old Beaufort and the waterfront park
items.why: Antebellum houses under live oaks and Spanish moss, where Forrest Gump and The Big Chill were filmed.

items.name: Penn Center on St. Helena Island
items.why: One of the first schools for formerly enslaved people (1862), and the heart of Gullah culture.

items.name: Hunting Island
items.why: The lighthouse you can climb, the boneyard beach of dead trees and the maritime forest.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (33 °C), mild winters (5-17 °C); azaleas in March; hurricane season June to November.
areas.sleep: The historic district, between the squares.

items.name: The squares and Forsyth Park
items.why: Oglethorpe's town plan of 1733: 22 green squares under live oaks hung with Spanish moss, down to the fountain of Forsyth Park.

items.name: Bonaventure Cemetery
items.why: Statues and oak avenues over the Wilmington River, made famous by Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil.

items.name: The oak avenue of Wormsloe
items.why: Two kilometres of live oaks leading to the ruins of a colonial estate.

items.name: River Street and a ghost tour
items.why: Cotton warehouses on the river, then the town's ghost stories by night.

items.name: Tybee Island
items.why: The town's beach and its lighthouse, half an hour away.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (32 °C), mild winters (2-12 °C) with rare snow.
areas.sleep: Midtown, or Downtown near Centennial Olympic Park.

items.name: Martin Luther King Jr.'s Sweet Auburn
items.why: The house where he was born, Ebenezer Baptist Church where he preached, and his tomb, in a national historical park.

items.name: The National Center for Civil and Human Rights
items.why: The civil rights movement, including a lunch-counter sit-in you live through with headphones.

items.name: Georgia Aquarium and World of Coca-Cola
items.why: One of the largest aquariums in the world, with whale sharks, next to the museum of the drink invented here in 1886.

items.name: The BeltLine Eastside Trail
items.why: An old rail corridor turned into a walk of murals and food halls, to Ponce City Market.

areas.season: Hot humid summers, mild winters; the colours in late October.
areas.sleep: Downtown by the river or the North Shore.

items.name: Lookout Mountain: the Incline, Rock City and Ruby Falls
items.why: One of the steepest passenger railways in the world, the rock gardens of 'See Rock City' with their view over seven states, and a waterfall inside the mountain.

items.name: The Walnut Street Bridge and the riverfront
items.why: A walking bridge of 1891 over the Tennessee River to the North Shore.

items.name: The Tennessee Aquarium
items.why: Freshwater life from the Appalachian streams to the Mississippi delta.

items.name: Chickamauga battlefield
items.why: The oldest national military park (1890), on the field of one of the bloodiest battles of the Civil War.

areas.season: Warm humid summers (29 °C in the valleys, 18 °C on the tops), the colours from mid-October into November, cool winters with snow up high; Kuwohi's road shuts December to March.
areas.sleep: Gatlinburg at the park gate; Townsend on the quiet side for Cades Cove.

items.name: Cades Cove
items.book: A parking tag for any stop longer than 15 minutes (daily or weekly, online or at the visitor centres)
items.why: An 18 km one-way loop through a valley of 19th-century churches, cabins and mills, with deer and black bears in the meadows.

items.name: Kuwohi, the roof of the Smokies
items.why: A steep paved path to the tower on the highest point of the park (2,025 m), formerly called Clingmans Dome.

items.name: The Alum Cave Trail
items.why: Through Arch Rock to the overhanging Alum Cave Bluffs, 7.4 km there and back; strong walkers go on to Mount LeConte.

items.name: The Newfound Gap Road
items.why: Across the park on US 441 to the gap at 1,538 m, where the Appalachian Trail crosses; closed after snow.

items.name: Chimney Tops
items.why: A steep 5.3 km there and back to a viewing point under the rock pinnacles burned in the 2016 fire.

items.name: The synchronous fireflies of Elkmont
items.book: Lottery on recreation.gov in late April
items.why: For about two weeks between late May and mid-June, thousands of fireflies flash in time.

areas.season: Summer 25 °C up on the ridge, the colours in early-mid October; sections of the Parkway close for ice and snow from December to March.
areas.sleep: Blowing Rock or Boone.

items.name: The Linn Cove Viaduct and Grandfather Mountain
items.why: The curving viaduct of 1987 hung on the flank of Grandfather Mountain, and the Mile High Swinging Bridge at the top.

items.name: Rough Ridge
items.why: A short climb on rock and boardwalk to the view over the viaduct, glowing red in October.

items.name: Linville Falls
items.why: Paths to the overlooks of a two-step waterfall at the head of the deepest gorge of the East.

items.name: Moses Cone Manor
items.why: A white manor of 1901 selling Appalachian crafts, with 40 km of carriage trails round it.

items.name: Blowing Rock village
items.why: A mountain resort town since the 1880s, with the cliff over the gorge where the wind blows light things back up.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (32 °C), cool winters (0-10 °C).
areas.sleep: Downtown near Broadway, or The Gulch.

items.name: The honky-tonks of Broadway
items.why: Live country music in every bar from late morning to the small hours, free, the band playing for the tip jar.

items.name: The Grand Ole Opry
items.why: The radio show running since 1925, live from the Opry House (some winter shows at the Ryman).

items.name: The Country Music Hall of Fame
items.why: Elvis's gold Cadillac, Johnny Cash's guitars and the history of the music.

items.name: The Ryman Auditorium
items.why: The 'Mother Church of Country Music', a tabernacle of 1892 and the Opry's home for 31 years.

items.name: A songwriters' night at the Bluebird Cafe
items.book: Seats released online, they go in minutes
items.why: Ninety seats where the writers of the hits play their own songs in the round.

items.name: Nashville hot chicken
items.why: The town's fried chicken in cayenne, from mild to unbearable.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (33 °C), cool winters (1-11 °C).
areas.sleep: Downtown near Beale Street.

items.name: Graceland
items.why: Elvis Presley's house as he left it in 1977, the Jungle Room, his cars and planes.

items.name: The National Civil Rights Museum
items.why: Built into the Lorraine Motel, where Martin Luther King Jr. was shot on 4 April 1968.

items.name: Beale Street at night
items.why: The blues street of W. C. Handy and B.B. King, live music in its clubs every night.

items.name: Sun Studio
items.why: The small studio where Elvis, Johnny Cash and Jerry Lee Lewis cut their first records.

items.name: The Stax Museum of American Soul Music
items.why: Otis Redding, Isaac Hayes and Booker T. on the site of the studio that made Memphis soul.

items.name: The Peabody ducks
items.why: The ducks walking the red carpet to the hotel lobby fountain at 11:00 and back at 17:00.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (33 °C), mild winters; the Juke Joint Festival in April.
areas.sleep: Downtown Clarksdale.

items.name: Live blues in a juke joint
items.why: The Delta's blues in the small bars where it was always played; music most nights from Thursday to Saturday.

items.name: The Delta Blues Museum
items.why: The blues of the cotton fields in the old freight depot, with the cabin where Muddy Waters grew up.

items.name: The crossroads of Highways 61 and 49
items.why: Where, legend says, Robert Johnson sold his soul to the devil for his guitar.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (33 °C), mild winters (4-16 °C); the houses open for the spring and autumn pilgrimages.
areas.sleep: In one of the antebellum houses, or on the bluff.

items.name: The antebellum houses
items.why: Longwood, the unfinished octagon of 1860, Stanton Hall and Melrose: the wealth of cotton, and at the Forks of the Road the slave market that made it.

items.name: The bluff over the Mississippi
items.why: Sunset over the river from the park on the bluff, and Natchez Under-the-Hill below.

items.name: The start of the Natchez Trace
items.why: The parkway of 715 km to Nashville along an old path, with the Emerald Mound of the Mississippian people.

areas.season: Hot humid summers (33 °C) with daily storms, mild winters (8-18 °C); Mardi Gras in February or early March, Jazz Fest late April-early May; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: The French Quarter, or the Marigny for the music.

items.name: The French Quarter
items.why: Iron balconies, Jackson Square and St. Louis Cathedral, beignets at Café du Monde and Bourbon Street at night.

items.name: Jazz on Frenchmen Street
items.why: Brass bands and jazz clubs every night; Preservation Hall for traditional jazz in a tiny room.

items.name: The St. Charles streetcar to the Garden District
items.why: The oldest streetcar line still running in the world, to the mansions and the walled cemetery of the Garden District.

items.name: The National WWII Museum
items.why: America's war museum, in the town where the D-Day landing boats were built.

items.name: A swamp tour in the bayou
items.why: Alligators, herons and cypress in the swamps outside town, by flat boat.

items.name: Whitney Plantation
items.why: The one plantation museum told entirely through the lives of the enslaved.

items.name: Mardi Gras parades
items.why: Weeks of parades and costumes ending on Fat Tuesday, in February or early March.

areas.season: Mild winters (8-20 °C), hot humid summers (32 °C) with afternoon storms; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: The historic district, near St. George Street.

items.name: The Castillo de San Marcos
items.why: The oldest stone fort in the continental United States (1672-1695), built of shell rock by Spain in the oldest European-founded city of the country (1565).

items.name: St. George Street and Flagler College
items.why: The Spanish colonial streets, and Flagler's Ponce de León Hotel of 1888 with its Tiffany windows, now a college.

items.name: The St. Augustine Lighthouse
items.why: 219 steps to the top of the striped lighthouse on Anastasia Island.

items.name: Anastasia State Park beach
items.why: Wide dunes and a quiet beach across the bridge from town.

items.name: Nights of Lights
items.why: Millions of white lights on the old town from mid-November to January.

areas.season: Mild winters (12-23 °C) with the sea around 20 °C, hot humid summers; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: Cocoa Beach, or Titusville for the launches.

items.name: The Kennedy Space Center
items.why: The Saturn V that went to the Moon, the Space Shuttle Atlantis and the bus out to the launch pads.

items.name: A rocket launch
items.why: Launches from the Cape happen most weeks; the beaches and the Titusville riverfront are the free seats.

items.name: Cocoa Beach and its pier
items.why: The surf town of the Space Coast, with the sea warm from April to November.

items.name: Merritt Island wildlife refuge
items.why: Black Point Wildlife Drive for herons, spoonbills and alligators; manatees at Haulover Canal; the most birds in winter.

areas.season: Mild winters (10-22 °C), hot humid summers (33 °C) with a storm most afternoons; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: Near the parks on International Drive or Lake Buena Vista.

items.name: Walt Disney World
items.why: Four theme parks, Magic Kingdom first (1971); a day for each is the usual pace.

items.name: Universal Orlando
items.why: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter across two parks, and the newer Epic Universe.

items.name: Manatees at Blue Spring
items.why: Hundreds of manatees shelter in the 22 °C spring run when the river is cold.

items.name: A swim at Wekiwa Springs
items.why: Clear spring water at 22 °C all year, and canoes down the river.

items.name: Winter Park
items.why: The boat tour of its lakes and canals, and the Morse Museum's Tiffany glass.

areas.season: Mild winters (13-23 °C) with the Gulf too cool to swim, hot summers with the sea at 30 °C; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: Anna Maria or Holmes Beach.

items.name: The Gulf beaches
items.why: White sand and calm water from Bean Point to Coquina Beach.

items.name: Sunset on the beach
items.why: The sun going down into the Gulf, a ritual every evening, with dolphins often passing.

items.name: The free trolley, Bridge Street and the pier
items.why: The island's free trolley from end to end, the old piers and the shops of Bridge Street.

items.name: Kayaking in the mangroves
items.why: Paddling through the mangrove tunnels, with manatees and rays.

items.name: The Ringling in Sarasota
items.why: The circus king's Venetian palace, his museum of Old Masters and the circus museum.

areas.season: Warm all year: winters 17-25 °C and dry (the high season), summers 25-33 °C with daily storms; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: South Beach, or Brickell and Downtown.

items.name: South Beach and the Art Deco district
items.why: Hundreds of pastel Art Deco hotels of the 1930s on Ocean Drive and Collins Avenue, facing the beach.

items.name: A beach day on Miami Beach
items.why: Fifteen kilometres of sand with the sea warm all year.

items.name: Little Havana
items.why: Calle Ocho, the old men playing dominoes in Máximo Gómez Park and a Cuban coffee at a window.

items.name: The Everglades at Shark Valley
items.why: A tram or a bike along a 24 km loop through the sawgrass to an observation tower, with alligators beside the road; best in the dry season, December to April.

items.name: The Wynwood Walls
items.why: Warehouses covered in murals by street artists from all over the world.

items.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
items.why: An Italian Renaissance villa of 1916 and its gardens on Biscayne Bay.

areas.season: Warm all year (winter 18-25 °C, summer 26-32 °C), the sea 24-30 °C; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: Key Largo, on the bay side for the sunsets.

items.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
items.why: The first undersea park of the United States (1963): snorkelling or a glass-bottom boat over the only living coral reef of the country, and the Christ of the Abyss statue.
sights: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park

items.name: The Everglades at the Anhinga Trail
items.why: Boardwalks over a slough full of alligators, anhingas and herons at Royal Palm, an hour away; best in the dry season.

items.name: A kayak in the mangroves
items.why: Paddling the bay-side mangrove channels at sunset.

areas.season: Warm all year (winter 19-25 °C, summer 26-32 °C), the sea 24-30 °C; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: Marathon, in the middle of the Keys.

items.name: The Seven Mile Bridge and the old bridge to Pigeon Key
items.why: The road over the open sea of the Overseas Highway, and beside it the old railway bridge of 1912, reopened to walkers and bikes as far as Pigeon Key.

items.name: Bahia Honda
items.why: One of the best beaches of the Keys, under a broken span of Flagler's railway.

items.name: The Turtle Hospital
items.why: A rescue for injured sea turtles you visit with the vets.

items.name: Snorkelling on Sombrero Reef
items.why: A boat out to the reef under its old iron lighthouse.

areas.season: Warm all year (winter 20-25 °C, summer 26-32 °C), the sea 24-30 °C; hurricane season June to November, the peak August to October.
areas.sleep: Old Town.

items.name: Sunset at Mallory Square
items.why: The evening celebration on the pier, with jugglers and food stalls, as the sun goes into the sea.

items.name: Duval Street and Hemingway's house
items.why: The wooden houses of Old Town and the house where Hemingway lived in the 1930s, with its six-toed cats.

items.name: Dry Tortugas National Park
items.book: Ferry or seaplane seats weeks ahead; the national park entrance fee is extra
items.why: The ferry of 2 h 15 min each way to Fort Jefferson, a brick fort alone in the sea, with snorkelling off its walls.

items.name: The Southernmost Point
items.why: The striped buoy 145 km from Cuba, the southern tip of the continental United States.

items.name: Old Town by bike
items.why: The flat lanes of conch houses and gardens, the way locals get around.
